target.title: fix(ios): cancel queued push-to-talk invokes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelled or timed-out iOS push-to-talk requests could remain in a serialized FIFO and later acquire the microphone. The original patch made queued waits cancellation-aware, but serializing stop/cancel behind a running one-shot capture could deadlock cleanup, and delayed timeout, recognition, background, or Voice Wake cleanup could affect a newer capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only capture preparation is serialized now. Start commands use a command epoch so cancellation removes queued waiters and invalidates suspended preparation; stop and cancel bypass the queue and interrupt immediately. Every capture has a stable ID that owns its Voice Wake lease, one-shot completion, timeout, silence monitor, recognition callback, and terminal cleanup.

The Talk manager centrally reports capture end to the app model, so explicit stop/cancel, failed start, timeout, background suspension, Talk shutdown, and transcript submission all release the same lease exactly once. One-shot start and await are separate, making external stop/cancel able to complete the original request without leaving a continuation behind.

No protocol, configuration, persistence, or public API changed.

## User Impact

Overlapping, queued, cancelled, backgrounded, and timed-out PTT commands cannot start a stale microphone capture or stop a newer one. `ptt_stop` and `ptt_cancel` remain responsive while another request is preparing or waiting, and Voice Wake resumes only after the actual capture owner finishes.

## Evidence

- Deterministic tests cover cancelled queue waiters, command-epoch invalidation, cancellation after activation, fresh start after cancel, external stop/cancel of one-shot PTT, stale cleanup and recognition callbacks, background completion, and capture-ID Voice Wake leases.
- Swift parser, scoped SwiftFormat lint, native i18n sync/check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh full-branch Codex autoreview passed after the lifecycle rewrite.
- Exact-head GitHub iOS/macOS CI and iOS Periphery will be linked in the pre-land proof comment.
- Hardware gap: no physical iPhone is attached to this host, so microphone/privacy-indicator timing is covered by deterministic lifecycle tests and exact public CI rather than a physical-device run.
